bib.title: Chapter 20. AI-Assisted Performance Optimizations and Scaling Toward Multimillion GPU Clusters (AI Systems Performance Engineering)

question: How can AI assist in optimizing GPU kernels and system operations, and what will scaling to multimillion-GPU clusters and 100-trillion-parameter models demand?
contributions: Case studies of AI-assisted kernel/algorithm discovery (AlphaTensor, DeepSeek-R1 at NVIDIA, Predibase GRPO)
Future trends: smart compilers, AI-run cluster operations, 100-trillion-parameter scaling

results.claim: AlphaTensor found a V100-specific GEMM method faster than cuBLAS on large matrices
results.setup: DeepMind AlphaTensor (2022), NVIDIA Volta V100, large matrices, vs V100-era cuBLAS
results.quote: multiplied large matrices 10%–20% faster than the standard NVIDIA
results.note: Chapter later says 'a 15% speed improvement'; also says algorithms remain experimental and not in cuBLAS.

limits: AlphaTensor algorithms remain experimental; cuBLAS has not adopted them (chapter footnote).
DeepSeek-R1 and Predibase results are quoted from vendor blogs; no independent method details, seeds or baselines beyond the chapter.
Per-pattern FlexAttention speedups appear only in Fig 20-4, not in the text.
Chapter says Predibase's environment optimized correctness rather than runtime, and some human oversight was still needed in the NVIDIA experiment.
Agent-1 to Agent-4 material is a hypothetical scenario; automatic pipeline parallelism and continual learning remain research.
Chapter expands GRPO as 'Group Relative Preference Optimization' (standard name is Policy).
practices: Integrate a verifier with a robust test suite (as KernelBench) so edge cases do not introduce errors in generated code (DeepSeek-R1 section).
Give an LLM tools to verify, critique and refine its output in a generate-verify-refine loop (DeepSeek-R1 section).
Reward both correctness and speed when training code generators with RL (Predibase section).
Embrace high-level compilers such as Triton rather than hand-tuning (Smart Compilers).
Maximize goodput, not raw GPU utilization, since a GPU 100% busy on redundant transfers is unproductive (Real-time optimizations).
Use low precision (FP8, FP4) with higher precision for sensitive parts, sparsity/MoE, memory-efficient optimizers and aggressive activation checkpointing for 100T-parameter scale.
Stay in an oversight role: set objectives, guardrails and handle novel situations (Real-time optimizations).

terms.definition: a model's ability to perform previous tasks degrades as it specializes in the new tasks
when a GPU is busy, it's doing useful neural compute
instead of performing one quick pass through the model before generating a response, it refines its output over a period of time
